anomalies.obs: On the MCU sheet (mcu.kicad_sch) the shared thermocouple SPI bus lands on the wrong ESP32-C3 GPIOs: the SCK net NET0019 (U3/U4/U5 pin 5) is tied to U9 pin 19 = GPIO3, and the three chip-select nets NET0005/NET0002/NET0017 (pin 6 of U3/U4/U5) are tied to U9 pins 18/20/21 = GPIO2/GPIO4/GPIO5. The only correct line is SO/NET0004 on U9 pin 26 = GPIO10. GPIO6 and GPIO7 (U9 pins 22/23) carry no SPI label at all.
anomalies.expected: Per the specification the firmware drives SCK on GPIO5 and the three CS lines on GPIO4/GPIO6/GPIO7 (MISO on GPIO10). The schematic should connect NET0019 to GPIO5 and the CS nets to GPIO4/GPIO6/GPIO7.

evidence.quote: SPI2 on GPIO5/GPIO10, CS pins GPIO4/6/7
SPI2 configured at 60 MHz, mode 0, with sck on GPIO5 and miso on GPIO10; three independent CS Output pins on GPIO4/GPIO6/GPIO7
mcu.kicad_sch: U9 pin19 GPIO3/ADC1_CH3 -> NET0019 (SCK); pin18 GPIO2 -> NET0005; pin20 GPIO4 -> NET0002; pin21 GPIO5 -> NET0017; pins22/23 GPIO6/GPIO7 unconnected
thermocouples.kicad_sch: U3/U4/U5 pin5 SCK -> NET0019, pin6 CS -> NET0005/NET0002/NET0017

anomalies.impact: The thermocouple SPI clock and chip-selects are routed to GPIOs the firmware does not use, while the GPIOs the firmware expects (GPIO5 clock, GPIO6/GPIO7 selects) are not connected to the MAX31855s. SPI reads would fail, triggering ThermocoupleFault and preventing the heater from ever being enabled.

parsed.summary: The power, heater, USB and value-level connections match the spec, but the thermocouple SPI bus is wired to the wrong ESP32-C3 GPIOs (SCK on GPIO3 and CS on GPIO2/4/5 instead of the spec's GPIO5 clock and GPIO4/6/7 selects), which would break all thermocouple sensing and therefore heater control.
